Emma — great to hear and thanks for the clear asks. I put together two concise options and added a proposed escrow + milestone mechanism that tends to work well for seed-stage teams: attached PDF has the line-item math and a one-page term summary. Quick summary below — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through.

Option 1 — 12-month Starter (fast entry)
- Upfront credits: $60k applied over 12 months (prepaid tokens/embeddings).
- Ramp schedule: 25% of committed monthly usage in months 1–2, 50% in months 3–4, 80% in months 5–6, 100% thereafter.
- Term discount: 20% off list unit price applied to consumption drawn from prepaid credits; 10% ongoing discount on post-credit overages for months 7–12.
- Failure to meet ramp: 45-day grace window. If committed usage not hit after grace window, credits are escrowed and can be released against future usage up to month 24.

Option 2 — 24-month Founder (lower unit cost)
- Upfront credits: $120k applied over 24 months.
- Ramp schedule: quicker ramp to 80% by month 4, full by month 9.
- Term discount: 30% off list unit price on prepaid consumption; 15% on post-credit overages months 13–24.
- Step-down protection: if usage drops below 50% of committed for 2 consecutive months, Redwood can offer temporary credit extension or a one-off top-up credit (case-by-case).

Escrowed credits & milestones (recommended for seed teams)
- We hold prepaid credits in escrow (contractual construct) and release them to billing as usage occurs. If ramp targets in schedule are missed, credits remain in escrow subject to a 45–90 day remediation plan.
- If Redwood misses agreed uptime/latency SLOs tied to critical routes, Redwood will issue pro-rated credit back into the escrow pool (service-level compensation).

Attachments: FastLeaf_MA_v1.pdf (1-page term summary + line-item math), fastleaf_usage_projection_aug2026.csv (your sample usage turned into a 12/24m projection).

Next steps: if you want a negotiable starting point, we typically accept a term discount concession (up to 5% more on Option 1) in exchange for a 6-month milestone KPI (e.g., 80% of committed traffic routed through dedicated pool).

Would you like me to send a redline-ready DocuSign link for Option 1 so procurement can start review?

Best,

Folks — forwarding the thread from FastLeaf. Quick summary and my ask:

- FastLeaf (seed, strong product) needs either a 12- or 24-month prepay. They prefer 12-month to move faster and asked for an aggressive 30% discount for months 1–6 on Option 1.
- They require credits usable across dev/staging/prod and escrow protection if ramp misses. They also want a small SLA-backed remediation clause.

My commercial recommendation:
- Approve Option 1 but allow a one-time concession up to 25% for months 1–6 (we already proposed 20%). In return, require a binding KPI: 80% of committed traffic in month 6 routed through Redwood dedicated pool and a signed 12-month commitment. Why: 25% still keeps unit economics reasonable for the starter profile and escrow + remediation limits downside if they under-perform. Offering 30% without additional commitment materially increases churn risk.
